headline: Veteran journalist and teacher Shahed Kamal passes away
summary: The son of renowned poet Sufia Kamal, Shahed Kamal was a respected figure in journalism and education.
details: Veteran journalist and teacher Shahed Kamal has passed away. He was the son of the legendary poet and activist Sufia Kamal.

headline_marked: Tk 5,745-crore project: [[Environmental groups urge scrapping Aminbazar plant]]
headline: Tk 5,745-crore project: Environmental groups urge scrapping Aminbazar plant
summary: Three organizations claim the North Dhaka waste-to-energy plant would cause severe air pollution and create a heavy financial burden on the government.
details: Environmental organizations CLEAN, BWGED, and BELA have urged the government to scrap the proposed Tk 5,745-crore North Dhaka 42.5-megawatt waste-to-energy (WtE) project in Aminbazar.
The groups allege the project would impose a heavy financial burden, worsen air pollution, and undermine sustainable waste management practices.

Hasan Mehedi, chief executive of CLEAN, stated that at 85% capacity, the plant would generate electricity at a purchase rate of Tk 26.79 per unit, which could rise to Tk 47-75 if utilization declines.
The agreement requires the DNCC to supply 3,000 tonnes of waste daily. If the DNCC fails to deliver this amount, it must pay US$50 per tonne of waste shortfall.
Experts argue this creates a financial incentive to generate more waste rather than promoting recycling and waste reduction.
Environmental concerns include the emission of approximately 411,392 tonnes of carbon dioxide annually, along with toxic pollutants like heavy metals, dioxins, and furans.
The organizations suggested that the same investment could instead install around 425MW of solar power, which would generate more electricity without fuel costs or harmful emissions.
caption:
A Tk 5,745-crore power plant project is being called 'environmentally damaging' and a 'financial burden'.

Environmental organizations CLEAN, BWGED, and BELA have urged the government to scrap the proposed Tk 5,745-crore North Dhaka 42.5-megawatt waste-to-energy (WtE) project in Aminbazar.

The groups allege the project would impose a heavy financial burden, worsen air pollution, and undermine sustainable waste management practices.

Hasan Mehedi, chief executive of CLEAN, stated that at 85% capacity, the plant would generate electricity at a purchase rate of Tk 26.79 per unit, which could rise to Tk 47-75 if utilization declines.

The agreement requires the DNCC to supply 3,000 tonnes of waste daily. If the DNCC fails to deliver this amount, it must pay US$50 per tonne of waste shortfall.

Experts argue this creates a financial incentive to generate more waste rather than promoting recycling and waste reduction.

Environmental concerns include the emission of approximately 411,392 tonnes of carbon dioxide annually, along with toxic pollutants like heavy metals, dioxins, and furans.

The organizations suggested that the same investment could instead install around 425MW of solar power, which would generate more electricity without fuel costs or harmful emissions.

#Bangladesh #Environment #WasteManagement #Aminbazar #Sustainability

Source: The Daily Star, Somoy News
